claim: Let \(X\) be a nonempty noncontractible finite \(T_0\)-space and let \(D_n\) be the discrete \(n\)-point finite space. For every integer \(n\ge 2\), if \(Z=X\oplus D_n\) is the non-Hausdorff join obtained by placing every point of \(X\) below every point of \(D_n\), then, in the unreduced Schwarz-genus convention, \(\mathrm{TC}(Z)=n^2\).

correctness.rationale: The upper bound follows from the \(n\) contractible principal opens and Tanaka’s finite-space inequality \(\mathrm{TC}(Z)\le \operatorname{cat}(Z\times Z)\le \operatorname{cat}(Z)^2\). For the lower bound, fewer than \(n^2\) motion-planning domains force one open lower set \(Q\) to contain two maximal pairs. Slicing \(Q\) at a point of \(X\) makes the inclusion of a subspace containing a two-top suspension null-homotopic. The explicit order-preserving retraction \(Z\to X\oplus S^0\) then makes the identity of that suspension null-homotopic, contradicting Kandola’s theorem that the two-top suspension of a noncontractible finite \(X\) has \(\mathrm{TC}=4\) and hence is noncontractible. The symmetric first-coordinate case is identical. All quantifiers and the unreduced convention are explicit; finite checks are only consistency tests.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an exact invariant for an infinite and structurally natural class of finite spaces: adjoining \(n\) incomparable maxima to any noncontractible finite base forces quadratic topological complexity \(n^2\). It simultaneously generalizes the arbitrary-base two-point suspension theorem and the arbitrary-size discrete-join theorem, isolates the maximal antichain as the exact motion-planning bottleneck, and yields immediate exact values for many finite weak orders and iterated join constructions. This is a structural extension rather than a parameter increment or finite census.
